answer: Each agent registers one timber stand on a ridge slope and posts an 80-credit bond. A spiral survey counts stems over the limit, and files a timber tally bound to one key. Auditors recompute it from the ridge map; a gap over 3 percent, a reused tally, or a second stand per key voids the claim and burns the bond. First fee 45; the kth stand under one key costs 45+6(k-1), so the 1000th costs 6039 and 1000 fakes cost 3,042,000 plus 80,000 locked. A rented cruise fails: a borrowed tally mismatches the filer and the spiral recount burns the renter's bond. Honest agents file once and pay 45.
